title: Submodule Fundamentals
description: Understand Git submodules and how to include external repositories inside your project.

data.text: Git submodules allow you to keep a Git repository as a subdirectory of another Git repository. This lets you clone another repository into your project and keep your commits separate. Submodules are useful when you want to track a dependency that lives in its own repository.
git submodule add clones an external repository into a subdirectory of your project and records the submodule's URL and current commit in your .gitmodules file and Git index.

data.title: Add a submodule to your project
data.code:
# Add a submodule
git submodule add https://github.com/example/lib.git external/lib

# This creates:
# - external/lib/ (the cloned submodule)
# - .gitmodules (records the URL and path)

# Commit the .gitmodules file and the submodule pointer
git add .gitmodules external/lib
git commit -m "chore: add lib as submodule"

data.text: When you clone a repository that contains submodules, the submodule directories are created but empty. You must explicitly initialize and update them.

data.title: Clone and initialize submodules
data.code:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/example/project.git
cd project

# Initialize submodules (reads .gitmodules)
git submodule init

# Update submodules (clones the actual content)
git submodule update

# Or do both in one step
git submodule update --init --recursive

data.text: A submodule does not track branches by default. Instead, the parent repository records the exact commit SHA of the submodule. This means the submodule is pinned to a specific commit, not a branch like main.

data.title: Inspect submodule state
data.code:
# See submodule status
git submodule status

# Output looks like:
#  abc1234... external/lib (heads/main)
# -def5678... external/tools (heads/v1.0)

# The leading character indicates:
# ' ' = up-to-date
# '-' = not initialized
# '+' = different commit checked out than recorded
# 'U' = merge conflict

data.text: To update a submodule to a newer commit, you must enter the submodule directory, checkout the desired commit, and then commit the updated pointer in the parent repository.

data.title: Update a submodule to the latest commit
data.code:
# Enter the submodule directory
cd external/lib

# Checkout the branch and pull
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Return to the parent repository
cd ../..

# Commit the updated submodule pointer
git add external/lib
git commit -m "chore: update lib submodule to latest"

data.title: Submodules require explicit updates
data.text: Submodules do not auto-update. When the submodule repository moves forward, your parent repository still points to the old commit. You must manually update the submodule pointer and commit the change.

items.question: What is the difference between a submodule and a subtree?
items.answer: Submodules keep the external repository separate with a pointer to a specific commit. Subtrees merge the external repository's code into your repository. Subtrees are simpler to use but create a larger repository.

items.question: Can I edit files inside a submodule?
items.answer: Yes, but you must commit and push changes to the submodule repository separately from the parent repository. The parent repository only records the submodule's new commit SHA.

items.question: What happens if I delete a submodule?
items.answer: Use git submodule deinit -f <path> followed by git rm -f <path>. This removes the submodule directory, the .gitmodules entry, and the .git/config entry.

items.question: Are submodules supported on Windows?
items.answer: Yes. Submodules work on all platforms. Use PowerShell or Git Bash for the best experience.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Submodules track external repositories as subdirectories
The parent repository records the submodule's exact commit SHA
git submodule update --init --recursive clones and initializes submodules
Updating a submodule requires entering the submodule, pulling, and committing the new pointer
Submodules do not auto-update when the external repository advances
